findings.F1: The test's result points the way the idea predicts but falls short of the bar: the mean unusual next-day fall is +0.51 % with t 1.65 over 804 cases on 412 days, and the idea's size is +0.72 % per case (0.152 of a usual move, t 2.05, 300 days).
findings.F2: In the folds shown (B, C), the effect is positive in every year (2018 +1.66 %, 2019 +0.87 %, 2020 +0.46 %, 2021 +0.60 %, t 0.47 to 1.49). It is also positive in 9 of 10 windows; the one exception is w11 at −8.6 % on only 9 cases. So it is consistent everywhere and too small in each part to show alone.
findings.F3: Five of six coins point the predicted way (BTC +1.28 % t 2.40, ZEC +1.41 % t 2.05, LTC +1.42 % t 1.82, XMR +0.66 %, ETH +0.48 %), and only XRP is slightly negative (−0.15 %, t −0.10, 47 cases). The weak t comes from too few cases per coin, not from one coin carrying the result.
findings.F4: The effect is graded at its deep end. The deepest quarter of forecasts gives +3.00 % (t 2.54, 94 cases, 51 days) against −0.41 % to +0.99 % for the other three quarters. The rank correlation of the forecast's depth with the next-day fall is 0.15, and step 5's deeper-minus-shallower check passed (+0.51 %).
findings.F5: The effect is a one-day effect, matching the plan's horizon: the unusual fall is +0.93 % at 1 day (t 1.74, 177 days) and fades to +0.32 % at 2 days (t 0.43), +0.03 % at 3 days and −0.47 % at 5 days (t −0.52). Another horizon would not make it clearer.
findings.F6: The size of the up day itself does not grade the fall. Its rank correlation with the next-day fall is −0.05, and the biggest-up-day quarter gives +0.12 % against +1.1 % to +1.9 % for the others. The prior 3-day fall carries the effect, as the idea says.
findings.F7: The move is large enough to trade. The total move per case (+0.59 %) is 3.1 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade, so what is missing is evidence, not size.

ideas.name: deep-fall bounce, all coins
ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, a coin's up day that comes after a 3-day fall is followed by a fall over the next day, and the deeper that 3-day fall against the standard deviation of its daily returns over the past 30 days, the larger the next-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorts the one-day bounce inside an agitated decline only for a day and sizes it by how deep the 3-day fall was, which keeps the book out of the shallow-dip bounces that made its deepest fall.
